skill.name: founder-content
skill.description: Generate a single LinkedIn-native post for a founder, on a specific pillar (Pillar / Proof / Process / Person) and using one of the 5 hook archetypes. Self-checks against the JMC voice rubric and banned-patterns list before delivering. Loaded by the main founder-brand skill when the user wants to write a single post.
skill.summary: Create concise founder LinkedIn posts with a clear pillar, hook, receipt, and voice review.
skill.author: cmj-hub

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives. The matches identify Markdown backticks, fenced code markers, and a documented relative reference, with no evidence of command execution or path traversal.

finding_verdicts.reason: The backticks on line 17 delimit an inline Markdown reference after the phrase "Loaded by". No Ruby expression, shell command, or execution behavior is present.
The matched text is a fenced Markdown code delimiter surrounding the workflow example. It does not invoke Ruby or an external command.
The matched text is a fenced Markdown code delimiter around the output structure. It contains no executable shell or Ruby operation.
The sequence is a literal Markdown reference to the documented founder-brand framework. No code reads a user-controlled path or performs filesystem traversal.

content.value_statement: Founders often have useful experience but struggle to turn it into specific, credible LinkedIn posts. This skill structures one post around a clear pillar, hook, receipt, and founder voice.
actual_capabilities: Selects a content pillar from Pillar, Proof, Process, or Person.
Matches the post to one of five hook archetypes.
Prompts for specific numbers, names, dates, or anonymized receipts.
Structures a short LinkedIn post with a hook, body, receipt block, and close.
Checks the draft against voice, banned-pattern, length, and hashtag rules.
limitations: It does not invent credible metrics, names, dates, or customer evidence.
It requires the user to provide a real receipt and framework connection.
It does not publish posts or manage LinkedIn accounts.
It focuses on one post rather than a complete content calendar.

use_cases.title: Turn a customer result into proof
use_cases.description: Provide a specific outcome, unexpected lever, and framework connection. Receive a concise proof post with a clear receipt block.

use_cases.title: Share a repeatable process
use_cases.description: Describe how you perform a recurring task. Receive a process post with scannable steps and a direct closing line.

use_cases.title: Shape a point of view
use_cases.description: Bring a strong belief and supporting evidence. Receive a pillar post with a focused hook and specific supporting details.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a pillar
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the best pillar for a LinkedIn post about [topic]. Ask for the missing receipt and framework connection.

prompt_templates.title: Draft from a receipt
prompt_templates.prompt: Write one LinkedIn post using the Proof pillar. Receipt: [specific result]. Unexpected lever: [insight]. Framework connection: [framework].

prompt_templates.title: Apply a hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this draft using the [Contrarian, Specific receipt, Confession, Pattern observation, or Question reframe] hook. Keep the receipt and remove generic claims: [draft].

prompt_templates.title: Run the voice review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this post against the founder voice rubric. Find the weakest line, check the receipt, close, banned patterns, hashtags, and length, then revise it: [draft].

output_examples.input: A founder shares that a sales process changed after three weeks of tracking follow-up timing.
output_examples.output: A concise Process post with a pattern-based hook, three measurable observations, the unexpected lever, and a direct close.

output_examples.input: A consultant provides a client result, timeframe, and connection to a course framework.
output: A Proof post that names the result and timeframe.
A short receipt block with specific evidence.
A close that points to the relevant framework without engagement bait.

best_practices: Provide numbers, names, dates, or specific anonymized descriptions before drafting.
Choose one pillar and one hook archetype for each post.
Review every claim for evidence, clarity, and a direct close.
anti_patterns: Do not request a post without a specific receipt.
Do not use generic openers, engagement bait, or more than three hashtags.
Do not combine multiple ideas into a long post with unclear structure.

faq.question: What type of content does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates one founder-voice LinkedIn post focused on a Pillar, Proof, Process, or Person theme.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the topic, specific receipt, unexpected lever, and connection to your framework or methodology.

faq.question: Can it create a post without metrics?
faq.answer: It can use specific names, dates, actions, or anonymized details when numerical metrics are unavailable.

faq.question: How does it choose the hook?
faq.answer: It selects from five archetypes and recommends one based on the chosen content pillar.

faq.question: Does it publish to LinkedIn?
faq.answer: No. It drafts and reviews text for you to edit and publish through your normal workflow.

faq.question: How long are the posts?
faq.answer: The workflow targets 200 words or fewer, with short sentences and no more than three hashtags.
